A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TKTO research work. All pages, including figures, tables, equations and appendices, are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Japanese TTS experiments, listening evaluations, token analyses and parameter sensitivity results.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds Chinese pronunciation experiments and evaluation with another ASR backend.

M1.justification: The contrastive models, original/flipped-label training, token weights and TKTO objective remain unchanged in Equations 1–6. Clarifying that the contrastive models do not share parameters documents the existing construction without establishing a procedural change.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates Japanese pronunciation ambiguity only. v2 adds Chinese polyphonic disambiguation using 5,000 sentences containing 行 and a Chinese speaker (Section 4.5), substantially extending language coverage while retaining the Japanese task.

E2.justification: All comparators in the original Japanese objective and subjective evaluations remain. The added Chinese and ASR experiments reuse existing comparison methods, including the base model, DPO and KTO; no new comparator is introduced.

E3.justification: The stated listener count changes from one in v1 Appendix A to three in v2 Section 4.1, without documenting whether evaluations were rerun. Added protocols specify 1.5K paired/4K unpaired Chinese samples with phonetic-checkpoint scoring, and paired-data evaluation with Parakeet. Original Japanese training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix D checks whether CER and bad-case improvements persist with another ASR backend. Section 4.4 also analyzes paired-data availability. Existing training dynamics, token-weight analyses, case studies and clamping sensitivity results are retained.

E5.justification: Uncertainty reporting practices remain unchanged: no seeds, repeated-run statistics, confidence intervals or significance tests are added. The increased listener count changes the evaluation sample size, not uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds Chinese results in Table 3, including unpaired TKTO accuracy of 0.898 versus KTO's 0.832, and Parakeet results in Table 5. Table 2 revises Base/KTO/TKTO NMOS from 4.15/4.21/4.26 to 4.09/4.17/4.21 alongside the changed listener count; these are not same-setting performance declines. Japanese Table 1, ABX and sensitivity results are unchanged.

T1.justification: New Appendix A explicitly defines the sequence-level KTO reward, KL reference point, value function and loss in Equations 7–10, adding formal background absent from v1. TKTO Equations 1–6 remain unchanged; no new theorem, proof or guarantee is supplied.

C1.justification: The introduction broadens its problem formulation from ambiguous Japanese pronunciation to ambiguous pronunciation generally. The abstract and contributions explicitly add the claim of using six times more training data, based on sample counts already reported in v1. The central method claims and 39%/54% performance headlines remain.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 replaces the explanation of paired training as overfitting undesirable examples with selection bias toward rare borderline cases. v2 also interprets the Chinese and ASR findings, discusses computational overhead, and more explicitly identifies unresolved scaling and architecture generalization.

D1.justification: v2 discloses separate contrastive-model parameters, approximately ten minutes on eight A100 GPUs for their training, and an explicit accuracy definition. It also identifies and links the Chinese phonetic and Parakeet checkpoints. Appendix B's existing training hyperparameters and implementation-source information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to DPO, KTO and TIS-DPO remain unchanged. Adding the missing Hall-E publication year is a bibliographic correction; the new checkpoint links provide implementation resources.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording clarifications, adds experimental subsections and KTO background, and moves subjective-evaluation instructions from Appendix A into Section 4.1. Most original prose is retained. The moved instructions introduce duplicated and incomplete scale wording.

P2.justification: v2 adds Chinese Table 3 and ASR Table 5; the original sensitivity table becomes Table 4 without changing its contents. Figure 1 labels are revised and existing displays are relocated within the same two-column design. The final appendix sentence spills onto an otherwise empty page.

improvement.justification: The Chinese evaluation and second-ASR check strengthen evidence beyond v1's Japanese and Whisper setting, while added cost and implementation details improve transparency. These are useful but bounded extensions of the same small-backbone, ambiguous-word study. Minor editing and layout defects reduce polish, but the added evidence supports a limited net improvement.
